name: Slovak
variety: Standard Slovak (codified norm based on the central dialects, as spoken in Bratislava and central Slovakia)
sources: Hanulíková, Adriana & Hamann, Silke (2010). Slovak. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 40(3), 373-378.
Kráľ, Ábel (1988). Pravidlá slovenskej výslovnosti. Bratislava: Slovenské pedagogické nakladateľstvo.
Kráľ, Ábel & Sabol, Ján (1989). Fonetika a fonológia. Bratislava: Slovenské pedagogické nakladateľstvo.
Pauliny, Eugen (1979). Slovenská fonológia. Bratislava: Slovenské pedagogické nakladateľstvo.
Rubach, Jerzy (1993). The Lexical Phonology of Slovak. Oxford University Press.
Short, David (1993). Slovak. In B. Comrie & G. G. Corbett (eds.), The Slavonic Languages. London: Routledge.
Beňuš, Štefan & Mády, Katalin (2010). Effects of lexical stress and speech rate on the quantity and quality of Slovak vowels. Proceedings of Speech Prosody 2010, Chicago.
contrasts: phonemic vowel length, independent of stress (sud 'barrel' vs súd 'court')
short versus long syllabic liquids /r̩ l̩/ vs /r̩ː l̩ː/ (vrch vs vŕba, vlk vs kĺb)
four rising diphthongs /i̯a i̯ɛ i̯u u̯ɔ/ (written ia, ie, iu, ô) that count as long nuclei
palatal /c ɟ ɲ ʎ/ versus alveolar /t d n l/ (ľ versus l is kept in the codified norm; many speakers merge it with /l/, especially before e and i)
voiced versus voiceless obstruents, including voiced glottal /ɦ/ paired with voiceless velar /x/
affricates /t͡s d͡z t͡ʃ d͡ʒ/, all four native
allophony: /æ/ (written ä, only after labials) belongs to careful codified speech; most speakers pronounce it [ɛ]

rhythmic law: a long nucleus (long vowel, diphthong or long syllabic liquid) is normally followed by a short one, so endings shorten after a long stem syllable (krásny, not krásný); the spelling shows this

/v/ is [v] before vowels, the glide [u̯] after a vowel before a consonant or word-finally (pravda [ˈprau̯da], krv [kr̩u̯], domov [ˈdɔmɔu̯]), and [f] word-initially before a voiceless obstruent (vták [ftaːk], všetko)
word-final obstruents are devoiced before a pause and before voiceless sounds (dub [dup], ľad [ʎat])
obstruent clusters take the voicing of their last member (kde [ɡɟɛ], nadpis [ˈnatpis]); /v/ does not voice a preceding consonant

across word boundaries and before certain suffixes, obstruents are voiced also before sonorants and vowels of the next word (vlak ide [vlaɡ ˈiɟɛ], dub rastie [dub ˈrascɛ]); prepositions s, k, z assimilate to the next word (s bratom [z bratɔm], k domu [ɡ dɔmu])
/x/ is [ɣ] before voiced sounds in these contexts; /ɦ/ is voiced
/n/ is [ŋ] before velars; /m/ is [ɱ] before /f v/
d, t, n, l before e, i, í and the i-diphthongs are read as palatals in native words (deti [ˈɟɛci]), but not in loanwords
short /i/ and long /iː/ have the same quality; mid vowels are open-mid
syllable_structure: (C)(C)(C)(C)V(C)(C)(C), with short or long syllabic r, l as possible nuclei
phonotactics: words without a vowel are possible (krk, vlk, prst, štvrť)
two long nuclei in neighbouring syllables are avoided (rhythmic law), with listed exceptions
in loanwords the letter sequences ia, ie, iu are two syllables, not diphthongs (materiál, diéta)
no voiced obstruents before a pause

stress.rule: Stress falls on the first syllable of the word; a monosyllabic preposition takes the stress from the following word; clitics are unstressed.
stress.cues: weak: slight intensity and pitch change; not duration or vowel quality

rhythm.notes: Traditionally described as syllable-timed; the alternation of long and short nuclei (rhythmic law) and consonant clusters add durational variability. The class label is an impression from the descriptive literature.

length.notes: Long vowels, diphthongs and long syllabic liquids count as long. The pronouncing norm sets long vowels at about twice the duration of short ones; in fluent speech the difference is smaller and depends on rate and stress (Beňuš & Mády 2010).

intonation.declarative: gradual declination with a fall to low on the last stress group (cadence)
intonation.yes_no_question: rise on the last stress group, highest on its final or post-stress syllable (anticadence)
intonation.wh_question: falling, like a statement, with a high question word
intonation.continuation: level or slight rise at the end of a non-final phrase (half-cadence)
intonation.accent_shape: stressed syllables are marked by a small pitch step; the main movement is on the last stress group of the phrase
intonation.notes: Terms cadence, anticadence and half-cadence follow Kráľ (1988).

tone.notes: No lexical tone or pitch accent.

problems: The rising diphthongs are read as two full vowels: ia, ie, iu become unstressed [i] plus a stressed second vowel (piatok [pi.ˈa.tok], rieka [ri.ˈe.ka], chlieb [xli.ˈep]) and ô becomes [u] plus [o] (kôň [ˈku.oɲ]). This adds a syllable and moves the stress away from the first syllable.
Some words whose only nucleus is a syllabic liquid are spelled out letter by letter (kĺb); others work (stĺp, vlk, krk, vŕba).
k is never voiced before a voiced obstruent (kde gives [kɟ]).
The prepositions s and k are not assimilated to the next word (s bratom, s otcom, k domu keep [s], [k]; the norm has [z], [ɡ]).
ä is always [e]; there is no [æ] (acceptable for most speakers).
Word-final voiceless obstruents are not voiced before a vowel or sonorant of the next word (vlak ide, chlap robí keep [k], [p]; the norm has [ɡ], [b]); only written voiced finals stay voiced there.
Only the default eSpeak tunes are used; wh-questions get the same fall-rise as yes-no questions.
The nominal long to short vowel length in the phoneme table is about 2.4 to 1 (290 vs 120).
good: initial stress, with some prepositions and prefixes joined to the next word
phonemic vowel length and long syllabic ŕ, ĺ as separate phonemes
v as [w] in codas (pravda, krv, domov, polievka) and [f] before voiceless consonants (vták, všetko)
final devoicing (dub, ľad, dážď) and voicing kept before a vowel or sonorant of the next word (dub rastie), which is the Slovak norm
regressive voicing assimilation inside words (nadpis, dcéra)
palatal ď, ť, ň, ľ, with softening of d, t, n before e, i and long exception lists for loanwords

notes: No formant, VOT or rhythm-metric values are given because I cannot quote published figures with confidence.
